what: Telegram challenges India ban over exam paper leak fears

clean_source_blocks.text: Telegram has taken the Indian government to court over its decision to temporarily ban the messaging platform days before millions of students retake a crucial medical entrance examination. The company challenged the decision on Wednesday, a day after officials blocked access to the app over concerns it had been used to distribute leaked exam papers. The government says the move will protect the integrity of the exam, which is due to be held again on Sunday after last month's test was cancelled over allegations of a paper leak. But Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has called the ban a "mistake", arguing it would punish millions of users while doing little to stop those responsible for the leaks.
Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has called the ban a "mistake", arguing it would punish millions of users.

Lawyers for the company mentioned the matter before the Delhi High Court on Wednesday, legal website Live Law reported. The judge has agreed to hear the case later in the day. The development comes after Durov wrote a post on X criticising the ban and arguing that it would not "stop anything", as those responsible for the leak would have already moved to other apps. Calling Telegram a "force for good", he said the platform had "removed hundreds of channels sharing leaked exam materials and related scams in India" in recent weeks. He added that Telegram was making its "edited" label more prominent to help prevent backdating scams. "Banning it - even temporarily - is a mistake," he said.

Millions of people in India use Telegram every day. Students join study groups. Businesses share updates. Friends and families stay in touch. Therefore, many users were surprised today (June 16, 2026) when reports emerged that India had temporarily restricted access to Telegram ahead of the NEET (UG) 2026 re-examination. The move sparked debate across social and professional networks. Some people supported the decision. Others questioned whether blocking an entire platform was necessary. So, what exactly happened? More importantly, why did the government take such an unusual step? Read on to find out. According to a public statement released by the National Testing Agency (NTA), the Indian government issued two temporary directions concerning Telegram. First, authorities restricted access to Telegram in India until June 22, 2026. This period covers the NEET re-examination scheduled for June 21 and the day that follows.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Telegram has taken the Indian government to court over its decision to temporarily ban the messaging platform days before millions of students retake a crucial medical entrance examination.

The company challenged the decision on Wednesday, a day after officials blocked access to the app over concerns it had been used to distribute leaked exam papers.

The government says the move will protect the integrity of the exam, which is due to be held again on Sunday after last month's test was cancelled over allegations of a paper leak.

But Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has called the ban a "mistake", arguing it would punish millions of users while doing little to stop those responsible for the leaks.

Lawyers for the company mentioned the matter before the Delhi High Court on Wednesday, legal website Live Law reported. The judge has agreed to hear the case later in the day.

The development comes after Durov wrote a post on X criticising the ban and arguing that it would not "stop anything", as those responsible for the leak would have already moved to other apps.

Calling Telegram a "force for good", he said the platform had "removed hundreds of channels sharing leaked exam materials and related scams in India" in recent weeks.

He added that Telegram was making its "edited" label more prominent to help prevent backdating scams.

"Banning it - even temporarily - is a mistake," he said.

The controversy stems from allegations that question papers for the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) - India's largest medical entrance examination taken by millions of students each year - were leaked before the test was held last month.

The case is being investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and more than a dozen people have been arrested so far.

[Lähde: OSTechNix]
Millions of people in India use Telegram every day. Students join study groups. Businesses share updates. Friends and families stay in touch.

Therefore, many users were surprised today (June 16, 2026) when reports emerged that India had temporarily restricted access to Telegram ahead of the NEET (UG) 2026 re-examination.

The move sparked debate across social and professional networks. Some people supported the decision. Others questioned whether blocking an entire platform was necessary.

So, what exactly happened? More importantly, why did the government take such an unusual step? Read on to find out.

According to a public statement released by the National Testing Agency (NTA), the Indian government issued two temporary directions concerning Telegram.

First, authorities restricted access to Telegram in India until June 22, 2026. This period covers the NEET re-examination scheduled for June 21 and the day that follows.

Second, authorities directed Telegram to disable its message editing feature in India for already-posted messages until June 30, 2026.

NTA says both measures aim to protect the integrity of the examination and reduce fraud aimed at students. More importantly, NTA describes these actions as temporary and limited in scope.

NTA officials found that several Telegram channels and groups claimed to sell access to the NEET question paper before the examination.

The agency says these channels targeted students and parents with false promises. In many cases, operators demanded thousands or even lakhs of rupees in exchange for supposed exam papers.

NTA maintains that no legitimate question paper exists outside the secure examination process. Therefore, anyone claiming to sell the paper before the exam is attempting to commit fraud.

As a result, authorities viewed these activities as a serious threat to students.

At first, authorities focused on individual channels and groups.

NTA says the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, also known as I4C, worked with law enforcement agencies and technology officials to identify and remove suspicious Telegram channels.

This approach helped remove many fraudulent groups. But, NTA argues that the problem continued.

When one channel disappeared, another often appeared in its place. Therefore, authorities concluded that channel-by-channel action alone was not enough.

According to NTA, this led to requests for stronger measures at the platform level.

payload.title: Telegram vei Intian väliaikaisen käyttökiellon oikeuteen
payload.summary: Telegram haastaa Intian hallituksen päätöksen rajoittaa viestisovelluksen käyttöä ennen NEET-lääketieteen pääsykokeen uusintaa. Yhtiön mukaan kielto rankaisee miljoonia käyttäjiä eikä ratkaise koepaperivuotojen ongelmaa.
payload.content:
Telegram on vienyt Intian hallituksen oikeuteen päätöksestä rajoittaa viestisovelluksen käyttöä väliaikaisesti juuri ennen tärkeän lääketieteen pääsykokeen uusintaa. Viranomaiset perustelevat rajoitusta huolella siitä, että sovellusta olisi käytetty vuotaneiden koepaperien levittämiseen, kun taas Telegram pitää kieltoa ylimitoitettuna toimena, joka osuu myös tavallisiin käyttäjiin.

## Kiista liittyy NEET-kokeen uusintaan

Intian viranomaiset estivät pääsyn Telegramiin sen jälkeen, kun oli noussut huolia sovelluksen käytöstä vuotaneiden koemateriaalien jakamiseen. Taustalla on NEET (UG) 2026 -pääsykokeen uusinta, joka on määrä järjestää 21. kesäkuuta. Aiempi koe peruttiin vuotoepäilyjen vuoksi.

Telegram haastoi päätöksen Delhin korkeimmassa oikeudessa keskiviikkona. Yhtiön asianajajat toivat asian oikeuden käsiteltäväksi, ja tuomari suostui kuulemaan tapausta myöhemmin samana päivänä. Rajoituksen kerrotaan olevan voimassa 22. kesäkuuta saakka, joten se kattaisi sekä uusintakokeen että sitä seuraavan päivän.

Hallituksen mukaan päätöksellä pyritään suojelemaan kokeen luotettavuutta. Intian National Testing Agencyn julkisen lausunnon mukaan viranomaiset antoivat Telegramia koskevia väliaikaisia määräyksiä juuri uusintakokeen ajaksi.

## Durov: Kielto rankaisee tavallisia käyttäjiä

Telegramin toimitusjohtaja Pavel Durov arvosteli kieltoa X-palvelussa. Hänen mukaansa rajoitus ei estä vuodoista vastuussa olevia, koska he ovat voineet jo siirtyä muihin sovelluksiin. Durov kutsui kieltoa virheeksi ja sanoi sen rankaisevan miljoonia käyttäjiä.

Durov korosti, että Telegramia käytetään Intiassa laajasti opiskeluryhmissä, yritysviestinnässä sekä perheiden ja ystävien yhteydenpitoon. Käyttörajoitus herätti lähdekatkelmien mukaan keskustelua sosiaalisissa ja ammatillisissa verkostoissa: osa tuki päätöstä, mutta osa kyseenalaisti kokonaisen viestintäalustan estämisen tarpeellisuuden.

Telegramin mukaan se on viime viikkoina poistanut satoja kanavia, joilla on jaettu vuotaneita koemateriaaleja tai niihin liittyviä huijauksia Intiassa. Durov kertoi myös yhtiön tekevän viestien muokkausmerkinnästä näkyvämmän, jotta takautuviin muokkauksiin perustuvia huijauksia olisi vaikeampi tehdä.

Tapaus jättää Delhin korkeimman oikeuden ratkaistavaksi, oliko väliaikainen rajoitus hyväksyttävä keino turvata NEET-uusintakoe vai suhteeton toimi miljoonien käyttäjien viestintää vastaan.
summary_bullets: Telegram haastoi Intian väliaikaisen käyttörajoituksen Delhin korkeimmassa oikeudessa.
Rajoitus liittyy NEET-lääketieteen pääsykokeen uusintaan ja koepaperivuotojen pelkoon.
Pavel Durovin mukaan kielto rankaisee miljoonia käyttäjiä eikä pysäytä vuotojen tekijöitä.
